ns1:channel.ns1:title: Communications Earth & Environment
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

ns1:item.ns1:title: A revised early Jurassic to Albian chronology for dinosaur evolution in tropical Asia
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04096-5

Sauropodomorph-bearing assemblages from the Khorat Plateau, Thailand, begin at least 20 million years later than previously believed, with subsequent faunal turnover paralleling that observed in Laurasia and Gondwana, according to detrital zircon U–Pb dating.
ns1:item.dc:title: A revised early Jurassic to Albian chronology for dinosaur evolution in tropical Asia

ns1:item.ns1:title: Forest loss is increasingly driven by international consumption
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04093-8

More than one third of global forest loss is embodied in international demand, with urbanization and manufacturing emerging as key predictors, according to a study that combined satellite observations with trade modeling and machine learning.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Economic incentives for conifers may limit broadleaf expansion in climate-adaptive European forests
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04087-6

Drought, is perceived as a major threat to European forests, and while professionals prioritize species diversity, broadleaf-conifer mixtures, and assisted regeneration, timber price increases may favor maintaining conifers, according to survey of forest professionals.
